contexts.text: Occurs. AC 1461.
Love from self and from the world, with which heavenly love can never agree; but there are also pleasures that quite agree with heavenly things. AC 1563:2.
Unless these things are first dispersed, the inward man can by no means agree with the outward.
There are two kinds of things with the outward man, namely those that can agree with the inward, and those that do not agree. Signified. AC 1568:2. AC 1568:4. Explained.
Strife between the shepherds of Abram's cattle and between the shepherds of Lot's cattle = that the inward and the outward man did not agree. AC 1572.
The agreement or union of the inward man with the outward. Explained.
How can these two forms, of hatred and of charity, agree in one place at the same time?

In the Lord's Kingdom a one is constituted of many various things so disposed by the Lord that they agree; the agreement or harmony of many is implanted by the Lord through their all having relation to him. Explained.
The agreement of the literal sense of the Word with the inward sense, is here treated of, consequently the agreement of the doctrinal things of faith... with the same.
Good... could not then manifest itself, because there were such things without as it could not agree with...
The inward and outward man... are reduced to agreement and correspondence through temptations.

Worldly and heavenly things agree with man when heavenly things have dominion over worldly ones, but they disagree when worldly things have dominion over heavenly ones; when they agree truths are multiplied in the natural man, but when they disagree they are diminished, yea consumed...
When good becomes the primary agent, the Natural begins to be illustrated by good, whence it appears what things therein agree, and what disagree.
Every unit consists of various things, and this through heavenly harmony and concord.
These men are peaceable with us = agreement, here, as to doctrinal things.

In the other life there must be concord and unanimity of all in order that they may be a one... to this end the thought and speech of one must agree with those of others. It is fundamental that thought and speech in themselves should agree in everyone in a Society...
The blessedness of the affections cannot inflow into the bodily sense... unless natural and sensual things have been reduced to agreement with interior ones.

All the elders of the land of Egypt = the things that agree with truth... Elders = chief things of wisdom, thus the things that agree with good, here, that agree with truth, for the things that agree with good also agree with truth.
Moses willed to dwell with the man = that they would agree... To dwell with anyone, is to live together, thus to agree.
Consociations take place in the other life according to spheres; those that agree are conjoined according to agreement, those that disagree are repelled according to disagreement.
If she be evil in the eyes of her lord = if affection of truth from natural delight does not agree with spiritual truth.
The agreement of the truths of faith with the things that belong to the literal sense of the Word is here treated of.
When thou seest the donkey of him that hateth thee lying under his burden = falsity not agreeing with the good of the Church.
There are falsities that agree with the good of the Church, and there are falsities that do not agree with it. Explained.
Seventy of the elders of Israel = chief truths of the Church or of doctrine that agree with good.
Homogeneous and concordant.
All homogeneous, that is, concordant.
Unanimous and concordant.
